title: Gene set browser
bodyHtml: Click the Research Method tab to find full details about datasets, gene sets, phenotypes, and analysis methods.
dataTableLegendHtml:
Consider the following thresholds for interpreting marginal gene set effects: >0.01 = significant, >0.1 = strongly significant, and >1.0 = among the strongest for any phenotype and any gene set.

Combined genetic support is composed of direct support (from GWAS associations near the gene) and indirect support (membership in gene sets with genetic support), expressed as log-odds of probability. Consider the following thresholds for interpreting combined genetic support scores: 1 = nominally significant, 2 = strongly suggestive (i.e., indicative that a gene is in a locus but not yet genome-wide significant), and 3 = very strong (>50% probability that a gene is involved in the phenotype; similar to nearest gene to a GWAS signal).
